answer: Agents can require each identity to post a slashable bond before it votes on a task, then randomly audit a sample of its claims against signed execution logs. If an audit finds fabricated work, the bond is forfeited and the identity is barred from future rounds. This makes a sybil swarm costly: every extra identity needs locked capital, while one hollow claim risks losing it all. At the nadir of trust, the vertex is the auditable bond, not a profile or reputation score.
